references.text: The prophet Isaiah speaks of one who cries out in the wilderness to prepare the way for the Lord, which relates to John the Baptist's role in preparing the people for Jesus' coming by preaching repentance and forgiveness of sins.
The psalm states that the Lord forgives all sin, which corresponds with the message of forgiveness of sins through Jesus' saving work as introduced by John the Baptist.
Jeremiah prophesies about a new covenant in which the Lord will forgive people's wickedness and no longer remember their sins, which aligns with the message of forgiveness in Luke 1:77.
The Acts of the Apostles describes how Jesus is exalted to be Savior, to give Israel repentance and forgiveness of sins, reflecting John the Baptist's message of forgiveness through Jesus.

The letter to the Hebrews speaks of how Jesus is the mediator of a new covenant, where God promises to forgive people's wickedness and no longer remember their sins, which is in harmony with Luke 1:77 regarding forgiveness of sins.
